companyDossiers.name: Science Corporation
companyDossiers.summary: PRIMA traces a route from Stanford photovoltaic research through Pixium Vision to an acquired program at Science.

stages.title: A photovoltaic retina
stages.text: Palanker’s Stanford research investigated converting projected light into electrical stimulation at the retina. The lab lists high-density photovoltaic prosthesis work in 2012.

stages.title: Pixium develops; Science acquires
stages.text: Pixium developed PRIMA. Science’s April 2024 announcement describes an agreement to acquire Pixium assets and ongoing clinical programs.

stages.title: Projected images become retinal stimulation
stages.text: PRIMA combines a subretinal photovoltaic implant with infrared-projecting glasses. Science’s separate Science Eye optogenetic program has a different technical origin.

timeline.title: Photovoltaic research publications
timeline.text: Stanford’s bibliography records high-density photovoltaic retinal prosthesis and fabrication studies.

timeline.title: Science founded
timeline.text: The company’s later Series C announcement dates its founding to 2021.

timeline.title: Pixium asset agreement
timeline.text: Science announces the PRIMA asset acquisition agreement.

timeline.title: PRIMA becomes the near-term priority
timeline.text: Science explains its prioritization of PRIMA alongside its separate Science Eye program.

changes.title: Acquiring a program changes the history
changes.text: The company’s founding date and the acquired device’s research lineage are different timelines. Retinal pixels stimulate tissue; they are not counts of independently recorded neurons.

gaps: The agreement announcement does not establish an exact transaction closing date.
This is the PRIMA branch of Science’s history; it does not assign the same ancestry to Science Eye, Biohybrid, or every Science platform.

companyDossiers.name: Cochlear
companyDossiers.summary: A university research program became an industrial partnership and a commercial multichannel hearing implant.

stages.title: Clark’s Melbourne research
stages.text: Cochlear dates Graeme Clark’s research to 1967 and its first research recipient to 1978.

stages.title: An industrial partnership
stages.text: Clark, Melbourne and Paul Trainor’s Nucleus Group collaborated to commercialize the research, with Australian government support.

stages.title: A multichannel hearing system
stages.text: The commercial Nucleus device followed the research implant. Its electrode array delivers patterned auditory stimulation.

timeline.title: Research begins
timeline.text: Cochlear’s milestone history dates Clark’s early research to this year.

timeline.title: Research recipient
timeline.text: The company identifies Rod Saunders as its first research implant recipient.

timeline.title: Commercial recipient
timeline.text: Graham Carrick receives the first commercial Nucleus implant in the company’s timeline.

changes.title: Stimulation is the channel function
changes.text: Cochlear channels deliver auditory information. They belong to a different engineering comparison from intracortical recording channels or sorted neurons.

gaps: These are milestones in Cochlear’s own history, not claims to resolve every competing worldwide cochlear-implant priority.
The source passage used for the industrial partnership does not fix its exact starting date.

companyDossiers.name: Bionic Vision Technologies
companyDossiers.summary: A multi-institution Australian bionic-eye program connects retinal hardware, vision software, and a cochlear-research lineage.

stages.title: A consortium, not a single lab
stages.text: BVA brought together Melbourne, UNSW, Western Sydney, the Bionics Institute, CERA, NICTA and clinical partners. Shepherd’s history also links this work to Clark’s mentoring.

stages.title: Research moves into BVT
stages.text: Melbourne identifies BVT as BVA’s commercialization company. CSIRO describes supplying vision algorithms and software alongside the implant development.

stages.title: A suprachoroidal system
stages.text: External camera images are processed into retinal stimulation patterns. The implant’s behind-retina position differs from PRIMA’s subretinal photovoltaic arrangement.

timeline.title: Suprachoroidal research program
timeline.text: Shepherd’s biography dates collaborative development with CERA to this period.

timeline.title: First trial recipients
timeline.text: CSIRO reports three recipients in the initial bionic-eye trial.

timeline.title: Commercialization support
timeline.text: Melbourne describes BVT as the commercialization company of former BVA.

timeline.title: Further recipients
timeline.text: CSIRO reports four additional recipients, with image-processing work continuing alongside the implant.

changes.title: Software and implantation site both matter
changes.text: Turning images into useful stimulation patterns is a separate engineering task from adding electrodes. This path combines visual processing with a particular surgical location.

gaps: The 2017 commercialization announcement does not establish BVT’s incorporation date.
Historical projected launch dates in the 2022 CSIRO page are not treated as verified current market availability.
